tagline: Pioneer in commercial quantum computing, delivering annealing and gate-model systems to solve complex enterprise problems
hero_kpi_rationale: The 'QCaaS Revenue' KPI is the primary long-term growth driver, as it reflects adoption of quantum computing via the cloud model, a recurring and scalable model aligned with the HPC/AI wave. It is central to the transition toward enterprise adoption.

kpis.name: QCaaS Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from subscription access to the Leap quantum cloud platform.
kpis.description: QCaaS revenue is at the core of the future business model, showing strong year-over-year growth.
kpis.signal: Massive growth in recurring cloud model

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from system sales, professional services, and QCaaS.
kpis.description: Total revenue increased by 180% year over year, rising from $8.8M to $24.6M, driven by services and cloud.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by services and cloud

kpis.name: Operating Loss
kpis.explanation: Operating loss in millions of dollars.
kpis.description: The company reported an operating loss of $100.4M in 2025 compared to $77.2M in 2024, reflecting significant investments in R&D and infrastructure.
kpis.signal: Increasing operating loss despite revenue growth

kpis.name: R&D Spend in absolute value
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses in millions of dollars.
kpis.description: The company allocates approximately $50M annually to R&D to advance qubit science and develop next-generation quantum systems.
kpis.signal: Massive R&D investment in quantum technology

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Growing headcount to support expansion of operations and R&D in quantum and classical computing.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on fixed assets for the development of quantum systems and facilities.
kpis.description: Investments in manufacturing facilities, test equipment, and R&D centers in North America.
kpis.signal: High Capex to support hardware innovation and expansion

kpis.name: Quantum Supremacy Demonstration
kpis.explanation: Publication in March 2025 of a quantum supremacy demonstration on a real-world problem in the journal Science.
kpis.description: D-Wave published a peer-reviewed quantum supremacy result using its latest-generation qubit architecture, demonstrating enhanced coherence and superior computational power.
kpis.signal: Scientific validation of proprietary quantum technology

kpis.name: Gate-Model Systems Launch
kpis.explanation: Planned launch of gate-model quantum computer in 2026, completing the dual-platform offering.
kpis.description: D-Wave plans to launch its gate-model platform in 2026, solidifying its position as the only company offering both annealing and gate-model quantum technologies.

risks.title: Ongoing financial losses
risks.score_rationale: The company reported net losses of $355.1M in 2025 and an operating loss of $100.4M, with an accumulated deficit of $982.0M. Management expects significant losses in the foreseeable future due to ongoing R&D investments.

risks.title: Dependence on R&D and technological innovation
risks.score_rationale: The company is entirely dependent on its ability to develop commercially viable and high-performance quantum systems. Design and development efforts continue throughout the systems' useful life. Any technological failure would severely impact business prospects.

risks.title: Commercial demand uncertainty
risks.score_rationale: The company is in an early growth phase within an emerging market and heavily relies on commercial adoption of quantum computing, which remains unpredictable. Realization of production quantum use cases is still limited.

risks.title: Increased competition in quantum
risks.score_rationale: Although D-Wave holds a first-mover advantage, numerous other companies and laboratories (Google, IBM, IonQ, etc.) are making significant investments in quantum technologies, creating intensified competition.

risks.title: Dependence on talent and rare technical expertise
risks.score_rationale: The quantum industry faces a critical shortage of qualified talent. The departure of key R&D or executive personnel would directly impact the company's ability to innovate and execute its business strategy.

risks.title: Immaturity of the quantum computing market
risks.score_rationale: The commercial quantum computing market is still in its infancy, with few profitable production applications. Adoption timelines and profitability profiles remain highly unpredictable.

risks.title: Volatility in capital structure and warrants
risks.score_rationale: The company recorded $270.5M in mark-to-market charges related to its publicly traded warrants in 2025, creating significant volatility in net income independent of business operations.

risks.title: Rapid growth and operational challenges
risks.score_rationale: An 180% revenue growth creates operational challenges in management, scalability, and resources. Expansion across four sites, headquarters relocation, and opening of new R&D centers add operational complexity.

ai_positioning.summary: D-Wave positions AI as a key use case for quantum computing, with a commercial demonstration of quantum technology used for AI model training. The company emphasizes its role as a pioneer in the quantum-AI convergence.
evidence: First with commercial customer use of its quantum computing technology with AI model training
Customers apply technology to address use cases spanning optimization, artificial intelligence, research and more
